content.title: About
content.content: French fries are deep‑fried strips or wedges made from potato tubers, a staple in school cafeterias and fast‑food outlets. Potatoes provide carbohydrates, vitamin C, potassium and dietary fiber.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potatoes were introduced to Europe from South America in the 16th century.
The first French‑fries recipe appeared in France in the late 19th century.
In Russia, fries are often served with mayonnaise or ketchup.
There are over 4,000 potato varieties, but high‑starch types are preferred for fries.
French fries are a common quick snack in many school canteens.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps maintain normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and protects cells from oxidation.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Energy supply
items.content: Carbohydrates in potatoes provide quick energy, important for growing students.

items.title: Beta‑carotene in yellow varieties
items.content: Yellow potatoes contain provitamin A, which the body converts to vitamin A.

items.title: High fat content from frying
items.content: Deep‑frying adds calories and saturated fat, which can affect heart health.

items.title: Salt
items.content: Frequent consumption of heavily salted fries may contribute to high blood pressure.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: High‑temperature frying can produce acrylamide, a potential carcinogen.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may be allergic to potatoes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: French fries are typically served hot, sprinkled with salt, and accompanied by sauces such as ketchup, mayonnaise, or cheese sauce. For a healthier option, bake them in the oven with a small amount of oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked fries in the refrigerator for up to 2 days in an airtight container. Reheat in an oven or air‑fryer to retain crispness.
